Woman amongst a group of people. She wears long coiled metal bracelets on her forearams and is wrapped in light coloured cloth. She is one of the wives of the Chief of Yansa.

Full length portrait of the Chief of Oting and his wife standing on a wooden platform. The man wears a tight waist-ring and a headdress decorated with feathers and animal horns. The woman wears numerous beaded necklaces.
Full length portrait of a man and woman. The woman is wrapped in light coloured cloth. the man wears a waist-ring and a crested headdress and holds a blade in one hand.
Man with spear, wearing hat with three points and smoking a cigarette.
Half-length portrait of a man with ear neck and hair ornaments. His hair has been shaved around his ears.
Three-quarter length portrait of man with grass headdress. He wears a European shirt, holds a daos (blade) and carries a basket on his back.
Full length portrait of a man wearing a waist-ring with a cloth apron over it.
Group of men, some standing some sitting on the floor, in front of thatched roof buildings. Most of them wear neck ornaments.

View of several Konyak Naga men, probably of the village of Longmien (now Longmeang), wearing only tight belts, carrying bags and baskets slung over their shoulders, and in the foreground several men working on the ground, possibly digging or reaping.

View of three 'effigies of dead warriors': short wooden poles, carved with notches at the sides and in the shape of heads and headdresses at the top, with a floral emblem painted on the front, in the Konyak Naga village of Angfang (now Angphang).
View of two standing stones and two larger flat stone slabs, said to pertain to the Konyak Naga people, in a clearing.
View of three large stone slabs for sitting and many smaller upright stones in the Konyak Naga village of Yunghong/Yonghong.

'Konyak morung, Kongan'(handwritten caption). View of two Konyak Naga men and a child sitting on a platform outside a morung (house for unmarried men) with a thatched roof supported by pillars carved with human figures, at Kongan/Kongon.

'Konyak / House of chief of Yansa' (handwritten caption). View of several Konyak Naga people standing outside and inside a large building identified as the house of the chief of the village of Yansa/Yanha (now called Joboka), with a thatched roof supported by wooden pillars, and with woven panels as outer walls, decorated with mithan (ox) horns and other objects.

'Konyak. / Wife of chief of Yansa.' (handwritten caption). Three-quarter-length portrait of a Konyak Naga woman identified as a wife of Shomwang, the chief of the village of Yansa/Yanha (now called Joboka), wearing ear ornaments, many small-beaded necklaces, a long robe and matching dress, and many bangles on her forearms, with five men standing around her in a mixture of European and Indian dress.

'Konyak / Young men of Longkong' (handwritten caption). Full-length portrait of two young Konyak Naga men, from Longkong or possibly from Zusa, with other Naga people sitting behind them on a raised platform.  Both men are wearing plumed headdresses, ear ornaments, loincloths secured at the waist with several thick rings or cords, many bangles at their wrists, many beaded necklaces, and a carved figure of a human head hanging on their chests; one is holding a dao (cutting implement) and a woven basket with beaded tassels, the other is holding a cloak or blanket.
'Konyak, / Defences of Longkong' (handwritten caption). View of a soldier holding a rifle with bayonet, standing beside palisades with panjis (sharpened stakes) at the village of Longkong.

'Konyak. / Man of Nokphong' (handwritten caption). Three-quarter-length portrait of a Konyak Naga man from the village of Nokphong, wearing short necklaces, cords or rings around his waist, and a knotted headdress.

'Shomwang chief of Yanha's wife.' (handwritten caption). Three-quarter-length portrait of a Konyak Naga woman identified as a wife of Shomwang, the chief of the village of Yansa/Yanha (now called Joboka), wearing ear ornaments, many small-beaded necklaces, a long robe and matching dress, and many bangles on her forearms, with five men standing around her in a mixture of European and Indian dress.

'The chief of Yanyu' (handwritten caption). Full-length rear portrait of a Konyak Naga man identified as the chief of Yanyu (now Yannyu) wearing a headdress with a rear board and beaded threads, ear ornaments, a large-beaded necklace, beaded bracelets at his elbows, an ornamented backplate at his waist, many calf bracelets of wire and beads, and a long tied loincloth, standing on a woven platform, facing several other Naga men, with a soldier half in shot beside him.

'Men of Zusa (?)' (handwritten caption). Full-length portrait of two young Konyak Naga men, from Longkong or possibly from Zusa, with other Naga people sitting behind them on a raised platform.  Both men are wearing plumed headdresses, ear ornaments, loincloths secured at the waist with several thick rings or cords, many bangles at their wrists, many beaded necklaces, and a carved figure of a human head hanging on their chests; one is holding a dao (cutting implement) and a woven basket with beaded tassels, the other is holding a cloak or blanket.

'Konyak of Saochu (?) / or Tobu side / Hutton' (handwritten caption). Half-length portrait of a Konyak Naga man tentatively identified as either from the village of Saochu (now called Sauchu, described by Hutton elsewhere as 'a Konyak village of the sub-tribe called Chagyik by the Changs') or from the neighbouring village of Tobu. He has a tattooed line straight down the middle of his face and wears tasseled ear ornaments and a neck ornament of boar's tusks.
